Question: My gross total income is ₹8 Lakhs. I gifted ₹2 lakhs to my mom for my sister's wedding preparations via an Unregistered Gift Deed. So, while filling ITR, what should I mention as my total income ₹6 lakhs or ₹8 lakhs?
Old_Answer: Your income is ₹8 lakhs and that is what you have to mention while filing your Tax return. I think you do not understand the concept of gift and gift tax. You are gifting ₹ 2 lakhs to your mother. You are thinking that this can be reduced from your gross income. No, it can’t be that way. This gift is tax-free in the hands of the receiver viz. your mother. Just because you gifted this amount to your mother does not mean that it was not your income. Hence it is taxable in your hand. On the other hand, your mother can show it as a gift received from her son (you) and hence tax-free, Please talk to a CA or tax expert on this issue, if you like.
Answer_with_writing_sample: In your case, you should still report your total gross income as ₹8 lakhs while filing your Income Tax Return (ITR). Why? Because the Gift Deed, whether registered or unregistered, doesn’t affect your total income; it simply represents a transfer of funds without any income-generating nature. Gifts to family members are generally exempt from taxes, but your income remains intact. Imagine it like this: you've got a cake worth ₹8 lakhs, and you slice off ₹2 lakhs for your mom's wedding preparations. That slice isn’t going to make your original cake any smaller in terms of worth; it just shows how generous you are! So, don’t get caught in the stress of deductions here—just report the cake as it is, and don’t forget to mention that sweet gesture of yours. Happy filing!
Answer_with_user_profile: When filing your Income Tax Return (ITR), you should report your gross total income as ₹8 lakhs, not ₹6 lakhs. The amount you gifted your mother, even though it is a significant expenditure, does not get deducted from your gross total income because it is not classified as a deductible expense under the Income Tax Act. Gifts to family members are not deductible, and thus, your taxable income remains the same regardless of the gift. According to Indian tax laws, any gift received from relatives, including your mother, is not taxable in her hands, and therefore, your act of gifting does not impact your own taxable income. In summary, while you may be financially contributing towards your sister's wedding, this does not reduce your taxable income; you are still required to declare your gross total income of ₹8 lakhs while filing your ITR.
Answer_with_full_information: When filling out your Income Tax Return (ITR), you need to report your gross total income before any deductions or gifts given. Therefore, regardless of the ₹2 lakhs gifted to your mother for your sister's wedding preparations, you should mention your total income as ₹8 lakhs in the return. The reason behind this is that gifts made to family members are not considered a deductible expense under the Income Tax Act. While the gift may not classify as taxable income for your mother under certain thresholds, it doesn't reduce your own taxable income or gross total income. Thus, for ITR purposes, you should include the full amount and then proceed to calculate any applicable deductions under sections like 80C, 80D, etc., if you qualify for those.
